sections.label: Protecting Critical Information Infrastructure
sections.summary: This passage states a first aim: strengthening protection of Singapore's Critical Information Infrastructure against cyber-attacks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: First, to strengthen the protection of Singapore's Critical Information Infrastructure, or CIIs, against cyber-attacks.

sections.label: Businesses using cloud computing
sections.summary: This passage states that about 60% of all businesses in Singapore now use some form of cloud computing technology.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Approximately 60% of all businesses in Singapore now use some form of cloud computing technology in their operations.

sections.label: Technology adoption rate growth
sections.summary: This passage states that their technology adoption rate grew from 74% in 2018 to 94% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Their technology adoption rate has grown from 74% in 2018 to 94% in 2022.

sections.label: CSA stakeholder consultations
sections.summary: This passage states that in developing the Bill, CSA consulted extensively with stakeholders over two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: In developing the Bill before the House today, CSA has consulted extensively with stakeholders over two years.

sections.label: Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill purpose
sections.summary: This passage states the Bill seeks to update the Act for shifts in the cybersecurity operating context and strengthen its administration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill seeks to update the Act to address the shifts in the operating context in cybersecurity and strengthen the administration of the Act to address operational challenges CSA has faced.

sections.label: Virtual computers definition extension
sections.summary: This passage states clause 3(j) extends the meaning of computer and computer system to include virtual computers and virtual computer systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 3(j) extends the meaning of "computer" and "computer system" in specified portions of the Act to include "virtual computers" and "virtual computer systems" which, in turn, are defined in new definitions inserted by clause 3(i).

sections.label: Regulating essential service providers using third-party CII
sections.summary: Clause 14 introduces a new Part 3A to regulate essential service providers relying on third-party-owned CII for continuous delivery.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 14 seeks to introduce a new Part 3A which will regulate providers of essential services who rely on CII owned by third parties for the continuous delivery of essential services.

sections.label: Designating CII located outside Singapore
sections.summary: Clause 8 inserts section 7(1)(a) allowing CSA to designate and regulate CIIs wholly outside Singapore if owned in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 8 inserts a new section 7(1)(a) which will allow CSA to designate and regulate such CIIs that are wholly located outside of Singapore, so long as its owner is in Singapore and the computer system would have been designated as a CII under section 7(1) had it been located wholly or partly in Singapore.

sections.label: Reporting incidents affecting other computers
sections.summary: Clause 12 amends section 14 to require CII owners to report incidents affecting other computers under their control and suppliers' interconnected computers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 12 will therefore amend section 14 to require CII owners under Part 3 to additionally report incidents that affect: one, other computers under the owner's control; and two, computers under the control of a supplier that are interconnected with or communicates with the CII.

sections.label: Regulating cybersecurity of STCCs
sections.summary: Clause 15 inserts a new Part 3B to regulate cybersecurity of STCCs, systems at high risk of cyber-attacks affecting national interests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 15 inserts a new Part 3B to regulate the cybersecurity of STCCs, which are systems that for a time-limited period, are at high risk of cyber-attacks and if comprised, would have a serious detrimental effect on Singapore's national interests.

sections.label: Regulating entities attractive to malicious threat actors
sections.summary: Clause 16 introduces Part 3C allowing CSA to regulate entities whose disruption or sensitive information disclosure significantly harms Singapore's interests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 16 introduces a new Part 3C, that will allow CSA to regulate entities that could be particularly attractive targets for malicious threat actors because of the disruption of the function they perform, or the disclosure of sensitive information their computer systems contain, will have a significant detrimental effect on Singapore's defence, foreign relations, economy, public health, public safety, or public order.

sections.label: Issuing cybersecurity standards and codes
sections.summary: CSA will be able to issue or approve cybersecurity standards of performance and codes of practice for ESCIs' cybersecurity measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: CSA will be able to issue or approve cybersecurity standards of performance and codes of practice to stipulate the cybersecurity measures ESCIs should have in place.

sections.label: New Part 3D FDI providers
sections.summary: Clause 17 introduces a new Part 3D covering providers of Foundational Digital Infrastructure service, the last new category CSA proposes to regulate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 17 introduces a new Part 3D, to cover the last new category of entities that CSA proposes to regulate for cybersecurity – providers of Foundational Digital Infrastructure service, or FDI service.

sections.label: Third Schedule FDI obligations
sections.summary: The Third Schedule covers cloud computing and data centre facility services, letting CSA set standards and codes and requiring designated providers to report prescribed incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: For a start, the Third Schedule will cover cloud computing services and data centre facility services as they are crucial to the functioning of a wide array of digital services that enterprises and consumers use daily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: CSA will be able to issue or approve standards of performance and codes of practice to stipulate to the major FDI providers that have been designated, the expected cybersecurity practices that should be in place.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: These providers will also be required to report prescribed cybersecurity incidents that: one, result in a disruption or degradation of the designated provider's FDI service in Singapore; or two, have a significant impact on the major FDI service provider's business operations in Singapore.

sections.label: Offence for using CSA symbols
sections.summary: Clause 7 makes it an offence to use CSA's gazetted symbols or representations without the Commissioner's prior written permission.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 7 will make it an offence for any person to use CSA's gazetted symbols or representations without the Commissioner's prior written permission.

sections.label: Time extensions and expanded obligations
sections.summary: The amendment allows time extensions for regulated entities facing extenuating circumstances and expands cybersecurity obligations on CII owners and four new classes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: With this amendment, we will be able to grant time extensions if regulated entities experience extenuating circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: If these proposed amendments are passed, they will expand the range of cybersecurity obligations placed on CII owners under the existing Part 3 and regulate four new classes of systems and entities for cybersecurity, while accounting for the varying degrees of risk posed to Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Commissioner civil penalties powers
sections.summary: Clause 20 lets the Commissioner bring a Court action for civil penalties with the Public Prosecutor's consent, supporting CSA's listed aims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: With a wider set of proposed obligations, clause 20 gives the Commissioner the flexibility to bring an action in Court for civil penalties with the Public Prosecutor's consent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The amendments will allow CSA to: keep pace with developments in technology and business practices; respond to evolving cybersecurity challenges in our cyber threat landscape; extend its regulatory oversight to other important systems and entities and use a risk-based approach to regulating entities for cybersecurity; and administer the Act more effectively.

sections.label: Mobile phone subscription growth
sections.summary: Mobile phone penetration grew from 740 million subscriptions worldwide in the early 2000s to more than eight billion 20 years later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Mobile phone penetration also grew rapidly, with 740 million subscriptions worldwide at the beginning of the 2000s and hitting more than eight billion 20 years later.

sections.label: Cybersecurity capacity keeping pace
sections.summary: Singapore must ensure its cybersecurity capacity, capability and legislation keep pace with digitalisation threats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As Singapore continues to progress towards digitalisation, there is imperative in ensuring that our capacity, capability and legislation in cybersecurity keep pace with and, where possible, stay ahead of these threats.

sections.label: Overseas systems as CII
sections.summary: The Bill empowers CSA to designate an overseas computer or system as CII if its owner is in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Second, this Bill also empowers the CSA to designate a computer or system located overseas as a CII and regulate it as CII, if the owner is in Singapore.

sections.label: Time for entities to implement
sections.summary: Entities must be given sufficient time to understand regulations, grasp obligations, develop strategies and execute measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Whilst there is urgency to proactively secure our critical systems, entities must be granted sufficient time for implementation to fully understand the regulations, grasp their obligations, develop strategies and execute necessary measures.

sections.label: Section 23 takeover authority gap
sections.summary: Section 23 lets the Minister direct countermeasures but does not explicitly grant authority to take over CII operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The current provision in section 23 allows the Minister to direct organisations to take measures to counter serious and imminent threats but does not explicitly grant the authority to directly take over operations of critical information infrastructure.

sections.label: CSA intervention and SAF DIS
sections.summary: Similar provisions could let CSA intervene in CIIs, and the question asks about protocols for the SAF's DIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Incorporating similar provisions in the Cybersecurity Act could provide a clearer legal framework for CSA to directly intervene and take control of CIIs when necessary to protect national security or the lives of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, while the CSA's regulatory and enforcement roles are crucial, in instances where national security is at imminent risk, are there any additional protocols for bringing in the Singapore Armed Forces' (SAF's) Digital and Intelligence Service (DIS), to manage the cybersecurity defences of CIIs?

sections.label: Enforcing extraterritorial CII judgements
sections.summary: The question asks how extraterritorial judgements are enforced on overseas CII providers whose owner is not in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, regarding sections 7(1)(a) and 16(a)(1), how will the Government enforce its extraterritorial judgements on overseas providers of CIIs if the owner is not in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If we are not able to enforce the laws overseas, what purpose do these extraterritorial provisions serve?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More proactive oversight measures potentially including direct access to provider systems may be required for effective supervision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: WannaCry, the global ransomware attack in 2017, rapidly spread across computer systems over seven hours, while the 2015 Ukraine power grid hack led to electricity outages lasting up to six hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If we really want to monitor with a deterrent view in mind, we need to have operational integration and develop our backstop capabilities.

sections.label: CII amendments and overseas systems
sections.summary: Amendments require CII owners to report incidents targeting supplier-controlled computers, and new section 7(1)(a) lets CSA designate overseas systems as CII.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The amendments to section 14 will require CII owners to also report incidents targeting computer or computer systems under the control of suppliers to the CII owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The new section 7(1)(a) allows CSA to designate a computer or computer systems located overseas as a CII.

sections.label: STCC and ESCI designations
sections.summary: The Bill introduces designating temporary systems as STCC and entities as ESCI to widen cybersecurity assurance for critical and important non-CII systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Lastly, the Bill seeks to provide wider cybersecurity assurance for Singapore's critical systems and important non-CII systems through the introduction of designating temporary systems as STCC in Part (3)(b) and designating entities as ESCI in Part (3)(c).

sections.label: Expanded Cybersecurity Act scope
sections.summary: Expanding the Act to supplier-controlled systems, offshore cloud essential services, STCC and ESCI will increase CSA's scope of work multiple-fold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: By expanding the ambit of the Cybersecurity Act from just on-premise CII to CII and systems under the control of suppliers, essential services on cloud – even when it is offshore – and also to include STCC and ESCI, the scope of work for CSA will increase multiple-fold.

sections.label: SingHealth 2018 cyber-attack
sections.summary: The 2018 SingHealth cyber-attack compromised personal data of 1.5 million patients, reminding of severe consequences for national well-being and public trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The cyber-attack on SingHealth in 2018, which compromised the personal data of 1.5 million patients, serves as a reminder of the severe consequences a cyber breach can have on our nation's well-being and public trust.

sections.label: Global cyber crime cost estimate
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum estimates cyber crimes cost the world economy over US$1 trillion in 2020, underscoring the need for robust cybersecurity measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Globally, the World Economic Forum estimates that cyber crimes cost the world economy over US$1 trillion in 2020 alone, underscoring the pressing need for robust cybersecurity measures.

sections.label: Singapore SME cybersecurity survey 2020
sections.summary: A 2020 CSA survey found only 34% of Singapore SMEs had implemented cybersecurity measures, and 35% experienced at least one cyber incident in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a 2020 survey by the CSA, only 34% of Singapore SMEs had implemented cybersecurity measures, leaving the majority vulnerable to cyber threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The survey also revealed that 35% of SMEs experienced at least one cyber incident in the past year, with ransomware and phishing attacks being the most common.

sections.label: SME incident response support
sections.summary: Proposes centralised support and pooled services for SMEs, and reframing incident reporting as supportive partnership, noting Singapore's 96% internet penetration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While time is of the essence in mitigating the impact of such incidents, many SMEs find themselves at a loss with no clear response strategy in such situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We propose that in addition to the structured reporting framework for incidents, which will be covered by the amended Bill, the Government could also look into structuring centralised support or pooled services for SMEs to turn to for incident response and advisory services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is therefore essential for the Government to foster the correct perception of incident reporting from one of compliance and potential fault-finding to a supportive process that provides real assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Incident reporting should be seen as a partnership opportunity between the Government and businesses, where each report triggers not just a compliance check but a supportive mechanism to help businesses address and recover from cybersecurity issues responsibly and effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This strategic shift will ensure that responsible businesses and SMEs, view engaging with cybersecurity frameworks not only as a regulatory requirement but as a valuable resource for enhancing their security posture and ensuring their continued prosperity in our digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Based on World Bank's statistics, our most recent Internet penetration rate is at 96% in Singapore, as compared to 66.2% average worldwide.

sections.label: Cloud computing security concerns
sections.summary: Cloud computing drives digital transformation with scalability, flexibility and cost savings, but a study shows 90% of organisations worry about cloud security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Much of what we are experiencing right now is related to how cloud computing has revolutionised the way organisations operate and is a key driver for digital transformation, bringing with it scalability, flexibility and, of course, cost savings, the most important factors for businesses today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But a recent study by the Crowd Research Centre, with over 250,000 members on the information security community on LinkedIn and leading cloud security vendors, showed that 90% of companies and organisations are worried about cloud security.

sections.label: CII monitoring and reporting clarity
sections.summary: The Bill is not specific on how CII monitoring will be done, risking under-reporting, and CSA should help create a standardised reporting structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Bill, as it is read, is also not specific at the moment on how the monitoring of CIIs will be done, which may cause companies to under-report for fear of revealing trade secrets or expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It will also be helpful for CSA to assist in creating a clear and standardised reporting structure that all companies, including CIIs, can adhere to.

sections.label: CII owners' cybersecurity duties
sections.summary: The Bill makes CII owners, such as water, electricity and banking services, responsible for cybersecurity and resilience, and requires reporting supply chain incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill holds businesses responsible and accountable to cybersecurity and cyber resilience, especially when the rush to embrace AI and new technologies exposes businesses to new risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Owners of CII, such as water, electricity and banking services, are required by the Bill to be responsible for the cybersecurity and cyber resilience of their systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CII owners must also be prepared to report more types of cybersecurity incidents, including those that happen in their supply chains.

sections.label: CII cybersecurity spending allocation
sections.summary: Suggests the Government could require CII owners to allocate a reasonable share of expenditure to continually strengthening cybersecurity and cyber resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Government could consider requiring CII owners to allocate a reasonable share of expenditure to continual strengthening of cybersecurity and cyber resilience.

sections.label: E-commerce scams and online act
sections.summary: E-commerce scams more than tripled to 9,783 in 2023 with close to $14 million in losses, despite government efforts, before the Online Criminal Harms Act passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The number of e-commerce scams more than tripled to 9,783 in 2023, with close to $14 million in reported losses by victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The rise in e-commerce scams comes despite concerted efforts put in place over the years by various Government agencies to combat this crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Shortly after, the Online Criminal Harms Act was passed in July 2023, setting out ex-ante requirements that online platforms must adopt to better protect their consumers.

sections.label: E-commerce complaints doubled
sections.summary: E-commerce complaints rose from 2,236 in 2019 to 4,366 in 2020, almost doubling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: From 2019 to 2020, the number of e-commerce complaints almost doubled from 2,236 to 4,366.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Act 2018
sections.summary: The Cybersecurity Act was enacted in 2018 and established a legal framework for national cybersecurity oversight in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Cybersecurity Act was enacted in 2018 and established a legal framework for the oversight and maintenance of national cybersecurity in Singapore.

sections.label: Amendments to CII obligations
sections.summary: The amendments add reporting obligations on CII service providers for cyber threats and enhance the Commissioner of Cybersecurity's powers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendments will also introduce additional obligations on providers of CII services to report potential and actual cyber threats, including those that may pose a risk to continuity of service, and will enhance the powers of the Commissioner of Cybersecurity to act against irresponsible providers or those who fail to meet the new obligations.

sections.label: Concern over ambiguous terms
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about the ambiguity of terms such as "sensitive information" and "function of national interest".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the intention behind these measures is sensible, I am, however, concerned about the ambiguity of terms, such as "sensitive information" and "function of national interest".

sections.label: Overseas cloud service providers
sections.summary: Many cloud-based service providers are based overseas, outside of Singapore's jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many cloud-based service providers are based overseas, outside of Singapore's jurisdiction.

sections.label: Strengthening Singapore's cybersecurity framework
sections.summary: Updating and strengthening the cybersecurity framework can better defend Singapore against cyber-attacks and ensure national resilience.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By updating and strengthening our cybersecurity framework, we can better defend Singapore against cyber-attacks and ensure the resilience of our nation in the digital age.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill is a testament to Singapore's forward-thinking approach to cybersecurity and its commitment to the safety and prosperity of our people.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Bill amendments and oversight
sections.summary: The Bill updates cybersecurity provisions and expands CSA oversight to STCCs, ESCIs and FDI to keep vital services resilient against cyber-attacks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2018, we laid the foundations to safeguard Singapore's cyberspace and protect Singaporeans online with the Cybersecurity Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A year later, in 2019, digital defence was introduced as the sixth pillar of Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Following up on these, the amendments in this Bill will update and boost current provisions, while expanding oversight by CSA to include Systems of Temporary Cybersecurity Concern and newly created ESCIs and FDI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The changes will strengthen the Government's regulatory powers to ensure that these vital services remain operational and resilient in the face of unrelenting and increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks.

sections.label: Bill powers and regulated categories
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Commissioner conduct on-site inspections, broadens reportable incidents, covers non-provider-owned CII, and adds STCC and ESCI categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Among its key features, the Bill empowers the Commissioner of Cybersecurity with the authority to conduct on-site inspections and broadens the scope of incidents that must be reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Importantly, it extends the definition of CII to include "non-provider-owned CII", therefore holding third-party vendors accountable when they manage essential services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Bill introduces new regulated categories, such as STCC and ESCI, to address emerging threats and evolving operational risks.

sections.label: Clarity on special cybersecurity interest criteria
sections.summary: Businesses want clarity on the specific criteria used to designate entities as of special cybersecurity interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses would like to have some clarity on the specific criteria that will be used to designate entities to be of special cybersecurity interest.

sections.label: Rise in Singapore data breaches
sections.summary: Singapore saw data breaches rise by around 319% in the past two years, totalling 65,702 incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have seen a significant increase in data breaches, up by around 319% in the past two years alone, totalling 65,702 incidents.

sections.label: Expanded CII responsibilities and new entities
sections.summary: The Bill expands CII owners' responsibilities and CSA oversight to STCCs, and introduces ESCI and FDI classes, including data centers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proposed Bill expands the responsibilities of CII owners and the oversight of CSA to cover STCCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Additionally, it introduces two new classes of regulated entities: ESCI and FDI, which includes data centers.

sections.label: Appeals and non-compliance fines
sections.summary: Entities may object to directions, appeal avenues are needed given financial implications, and non-compliance fines are set at 10% of total revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: While entities have the option to object to such directions, it is essential to provide avenues for appeal, especially considering the potential financial implications for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: That said, I strongly support that the fine for non-compliance is set at 10% of the total revenue of the company.

sections.label: Past cyber incidents in Singapore
sections.summary: Lists cyber incidents from 2018 to 2024 involving stolen data, espionage and ransomware.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In 2018, SingHealth data breach, where the personal data of 1.5 million patients were stolen by a deliberate, targeted and well-planned cyber-attack; in 2021, National University of Singapore Society data breach, where the personal data over 1,300 members were compromised; in 2023, cyber-attack against the Marina Bay Sands that led to the theft of 665,000 customers' data; in February 2024, cyber espionage incident that took place during the Singapore Airshow period, which resulted in a foreign military phone call being leaked abroad; and even more recently, in April 2024, a ransomware attack on a local law firm.

sections.label: Bill changes to Cybersecurity Act
sections.summary: The Bill implements changes to the Act, including Clause 16 regulating ESCIs and empowering the Commissioner to designate them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In broad terms, this Bill seeks to implement several changes to the Act that would enhance the security of CII operators' supply chains, regulate the usage of cloud services, regulation of systems used for and during key events and designating ESCI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Clause 16 of this Bill inserts a new Part (3)(c), which regulates the ESCIs, including by empowering the Commissioner of Cybersecurity to designate entities ESCIs and impose cybersecurity obligations on them.

sections.label: Commissioner's civil and monetary penalties
sections.summary: The Commissioner may recommend civil penalties in lieu of criminal penalties and impose monetary penalties on non-complying FDI providers and ESCIs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Commissioner will be able to recommend civil penalties in lieu of criminal penalties for all offences committed by regulated entitles where appropriate and impose monetary penalties on non-complying FDI providers and ESCIs.

sections.label: Digital infrastructure providers' cybersecurity responsibility
sections.summary: The amendment requires companies providing foundational digital infrastructure services to shoulder more responsibility for their cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendment will require companies that provide digital infrastructure services that are foundational to our economy or way of life, to shoulder more responsibility for the cybersecurity of their digital infrastructure.

sections.label: Reporting peripheral system incidents
sections.summary: Owners must report incidents targeting systems peripheral to the CII, including third-parties and supply chain entities such as cloud computing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the amendments, owners will, however, also have to report incidents targeting systems that are peripheral to the CII, including those from third-parties and entities in the supply chain, like in the case of the use of cloud computing.

sections.label: ESCI disruption effects on Singapore
sections.summary: ESCI disruption could adversely affect Singapore's defence, foreign relations, economy, public health, public safety or public order.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: ESCIs hold sensitive information or perform a function of national interest so disruption to their services could potentially have adverse effects on the defence, foreign relations, economy, public health, public safety or public order of Singapore.

sections.label: Cloud deployment and accountability concerns
sections.summary: The speaker notes accountability complications with third-party cloud services but supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although the new Bill requires at least one of the physical computing resources of the cloud service provider that support the virtual system to be deployed locally, the question remains whether the risk can be well-managed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although CII operators in essential service sectors remain answerable to CSA for any lapses, the shared nature of digital services complicates the accountability framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that there are no overlapping roles or responsibilities, especially when third-party cloud services are involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my considerations raised, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Synapxe DDoS attack downtime
sections.summary: Synapxe, supporting 46 public healthcare institutions and 1,400 community partners, suffered a DDoS attack in November 2023 causing seven-hour website downtime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a case in point, Synapxe, the national health technology provider that supports 46 public healthcare institutions and 1,400 community partners like nursing homes and general practitioners in Singapore, was subjected to a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack in November 2023, which led to a seven-hour downtime in accessing the websites of public hospitals.

sections.label: CII owners monitoring overseas vendors
sections.summary: The speaker asks how Government will help CII owners oversee overseas vendors not obliged to disclose cyber incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I am supportive that the expanded coverage of the Bill which will allow the CSA to become more aware of the types of cyber threats that Singapore faces, the expanded coverage of the Bill will also impose significant responsibilities on CII owners to monitor systems that are currently owned by their vendors, which could be, at this juncture, beyond their immediate or direct control and supervision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How would the Government, in this instance, support the owners of CII to exercise oversight on these overseas vendors and suppliers, especially if these suppliers and vendors are not obliged by their own local laws to disclose instances of cyber incidents to CII owners in Singapore?

sections.label: Whitelist of STCC vendors
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Government will set up a whitelist of STCC vendors and appoint them without public tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Government, in this instance, consider setting up a whitelist of STCCs vendors and help them secure their systems ahead of time and appoint them directly for future joint projects without a public tender?

sections.label: Compliance cost considerations and assistance
sections.summary: The speaker asks about cost considerations in drafting the Bill, expected compliance cost increases, and assistance plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, can the Government elaborate on the specific cost considerations that informed the drafting of the Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the expected increase in compliance costs for businesses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are there plans to provide assistance to businesses to help them cope with the increased costs?

sections.label: Resources for SME compliance
sections.summary: The speaker asks what resources are available and urges a clear plan to help SMEs comply, including financial support or guidance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share what resources are available to assist businesses in complying with these requirements?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to outline a clear plan on how it will help SMEs comply with the new requirements, including any provision of financial support or specialised guidance.

sections.label: Cybersecurity amendments innovation international alignment
sections.summary: The passage states amendments must not stifle innovation and that international alignment is imperative for cross-border cybersecurity threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While acknowledging the importance of leveraging new technologies in maintaining Singapore's competitive edge, it is equally critical to ensure that the amendments do not stifle innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Moreover, in a world where cybersecurity threats transcend borders, international alignment is imperative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Addressing the cross-border aspect of cybersecurity is vital, so that service providers are held accountable for breaches occurring in overseas facilities that impact services in Singapore.

sections.label: Legally binding commitments Singapore law
sections.summary: The passage asks if legally binding commitments under new sections 16A and 16F must be governed by Singapore law and enforceable in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new sections 16A and 16F require designated providers to obtain legally binding commitments to provide certain information and notifications and to maintain certain standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry confirm that the legally binding commitment must be stated to be governed by Singapore law, subject to the jurisdiction of the Singapore courts and be enforceable in Singapore?

sections.label: Consultation concerns confidential business information
sections.summary: The passage states respondents to the public consultation raised concerns about extensive powers to obtain the CII owner's business confidential information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Respondents to the public consultation raised concerns about the use of such extensive powers to obtain the CII owner's business confidential information.

sections.label: Steps to protect respondent information
sections.summary: The passage asks the Senior Minister of State to elaborate on steps to protect information obtained from respondents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State elaborate on what steps will be taken to protect information obtained from respondents?

sections.label: Opportunity to challenge Commissioner's belief
sections.summary: The passage asks if the entity will be given the opportunity to make representations or challenge the grounds of the Commissioner's belief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if the entity will be given the opportunity to make representations or to challenge the grounds of the Commissioner's belief?

sections.label: No obligations on business community
sections.summary: The passage clarifies that neither the Cybersecurity Act nor the proposed amendments impose cybersecurity obligations on the business community at large.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To clarify, neither the Cybersecurity Act nor the amendments proposed in this Bill impose cybersecurity obligations on the business community at large.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Act entity obligations
sections.summary: The amended Cybersecurity Act imposes obligations on only four groups of entities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: With the amendments covered in the Bill, the Cybersecurity Act will only be imposing obligations on four groups of entities.

sections.label: FDI services providers obligations
sections.summary: The last group is major FDI services providers, because disruption could affect Singapore-based organisations and Singaporeans relying on them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The last group comprises major providers of FDI services because disruption to these FDI services – the services that FDI services provide – could have knock-on effect, disrupting to Singapore-based organisations and the lives of Singaporeans who rely on them for business operations, work and day-to-day living.

sections.label: Reported cyber-attack costs
sections.summary: Some reports say the average cyber-attack cost for organisations over one thousand employees is about $71,000, and one in eight firms suffered S$330,000 or more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: According to some reports, the average cost of a cyber-attack on an organisation with more than one thousand employees is around $71,000; and one in eight firms suffered costs of S$330,000 or more.

sections.label: National security attack consideration
sections.summary: The key consideration is whether a cyber-attack could seriously affect national security or national interests, so CII incident reporting requirements are expanded.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The key consideration is whether a cyber-attack on the entity could have serious implications on our national security or other national interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For instance, we are proposing the expansion of the incident reporting requirements for CII owners under Part 3 because the evidence shows that malicious actors are using CII-adjacent systems and supply chains to attack the CII; and so, we need to stay situationally aware of what is happening around the CII in order to keep the CII itself safe.

sections.label: CSA compelling mitigation measures
sections.summary: The Act and Bill let CSA compel regulated entities to mitigate cyber risk regardless of technologies used by entities or malicious actors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Act and this Bill allow CSA to compel regulated entities to take the necessary measures to mitigate cyber risk regardless of the technologies used by the regulated entities or by the malicious actors to perpetuate their attacks.

sections.label: CII supply chain reporting responsibility
sections.summary: CII owners must be situationally aware of supply chain attacks and report incidents to CSA; the Government deliberately did not compel all suppliers to report directly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: That means that it is in their interest, and it is also their responsibility to be situationally aware of supply chain attacks that could affect their CII and report such incidents to CSA when they become aware of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It was a deliberate decision on the Government's part not to compel reporting of cybersecurity incidents from all the suppliers of a CII owner to CSA directly.

sections.label: Directing stop of third-party systems
sections.summary: CSA could direct essential services providers to stop using a third party's system if the third party is unwilling or unable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Where the third-party is unwilling or unable, as Mr Darryl David noted could happen, CSA could direct the provider of essential services to stop using the system owned by that third party under the provisions in new sections 16E(2), 16H(2), 16I(2) and 16J(2).

sections.label: Prescribed incident reporting for FDI providers
sections.summary: New section 18M requires reporting only of prescribed incidents disrupting or degrading a designated provider's FDI service or significantly impacting its Singapore business operations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Rather, the new section 18M will require them to report only prescribed incidents that result in the disruption or degradation of the designated provider's FDI service in Singapore or has a significant impact on the designated provider's business operations in Singapore.

sections.label: Factors for non-compliance penalties
sections.summary: In recommending penalties to the Public Prosecutor, CSA will consider factors including risks created by the non-compliance, egregiousness and facts of the case.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Ms Hany Soh asked what factors would be taken into consideration on the penalties to impose for non-compliance – in making a recommendation to the Public Prosecutor, CSA will consider a range of factors, including the risks created by the non-compliance, egregiousness and facts of the case.

sections.label: Appointing person to accept service
sections.summary: New section 18G(6) requires a designated major FDI service provider located outside Singapore to appoint a person in Singapore to accept service of notices or directions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To facilitate enforcement, the new section 18G(6) requires a designated major FDI service provider who is located outside of Singapore, to appoint a person in Singapore to accept service of notices or directions under the Act.

sections.label: CSA powers against cybersecurity threats
sections.summary: Part 4 of the 2018 Act provides CSA powers to respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents and secure threatened or attacked systems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Part 4 of the 2018 Act already provides CSA with the necessary powers to respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents and to take appropriate measures to secure the threatened or attacked system.

sections.label: Appeal mechanism extended to providers
sections.summary: A regulated entity may appeal CSA decisions, orders, directions, codes of practice and standards, and this mechanism will extend to providers of essential services, STCC owners, ESCI and major FDI providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: A regulated entity may also appeal against CSA's decisions, orders and directions, as well as codes of practice and standards of performance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This appeal mechanism was created in the 2018 Act to protect regulated CII owners and will be extended to cover providers of essential services under Part 3A, STCC owners, ESCI and major FDI providers as well.

sections.label: CSA resourcing after Bill
sections.summary: If the Bill is passed, the Government will ensure CSA is resourced accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If the Bill is passed, the Government will ensure that CSA is resourced accordingly.

sections.label: CSA track record and cyber threats
sections.summary: CSA has administered the Cybersecurity Act well for six years, with no appeals, while national defences must improve against growing cyber threats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: CSA has had a good track record in administering the Cybersecurity Act over the past six years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: CSA works closely with the regulated entities to address their needs and concerns and, to date, no appeals have been made against CSA's decisions, orders or directions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: At the national level, we must continually improve our defences against cyber threats that are growing in scale and sophistication.

sections.label: CII cybersecurity and step-in orders
sections.summary: Cybersecurity of CII must be part of the CII operator's operations, so a step-in operator would take on that responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To be clear, the way that the cybersecurity of CII is dealt with has to be part of the operations of the CII operator.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, in the example that he has cited, the step-in orders for bus functions, for example, if that function and the systems associated with that function were designated as part of a CII, then the operator that steps in would have to take on that responsibility as part of its duties to discharge that function.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And that already is part of how the sectoral regulators for each domain, who are also the sectoral regulators of cybersecurity, regulate the domains.
